Task: Explain why the sky appears blue, in three sentences.

steps.action:
When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in all directions through a process called Rayleigh scattering. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than other colors in the visible spectrum, causing it to scatter far more strongly — roughly ten times more than red light. As a result, when we look at any part of the sky away from the sun, our eyes receive this scattered blue light from all directions, making the sky appear blue.
